Fig. 1.3.3 Anaphase d. Telophase (G. 'telo' = end; 'phasis' = stage): Telophase, also known as the reorganization phase, is reverse of prophase. It is characterized by the following key events: i. Daughter chromosomes reach their respective poles, and as they do, they decondense through hydration and despiraling, transforming into long, thread -like chromatin fibers. ii. Spindle fibers disappear while nucleolus and nuclear membrane reappear around each set of chromsomes. iii. By the end of the phase, two daughter nuclei form at each pole.

Fig. 1.3.3 Telophase 2. Cytokinesis: In this process, cytoplasm splits into two halves. It happens through the creation of a cell plate between two new daughter nuclei or through peripheral furrowing. Biology, Grade 11 | 71
Fig. 1.3.4 Cytokinesis in animal and plant cell

a. Formation of cell plate: In plant cells, cytokinesis involves the formation of a cell plate. Small granular bodies which are components of the Golgi complex and endoplasmic reticulum called phragmoplasts which gather at the cell's equator to form the cell plate.

b. Furrowing: In bacteria, fungi, and animals, cytokinesis occurs through furrowing. Here, the gradual appearance of a peripheral cleavage furrow between the two daughter nuclei. The furrow deepens, and when its edges meet at the cell's center, the protoplasm divides into two daughter cells.
Fig. 1.3.3 Cytokinesis (Cell plate method in plant cells) Significance of mitosis
1. Mitosis helps in growth of multicellular organisms from a zygote into an adult. 2. Mitosis is crucial for asexual reproduction in certain organisms, via fragmentation,

budding, and stem cutting. 3. Mitosis ensures genetic stability by maintaining a consistent number of chromosomes in daughter cells. 4. Mitosis contributes to cell repair, regeneration, and heal wounds. 5. Mitosis controls cell size by inducing the division of overgrown cells. 6. Mitosis guarantees qualitatively and quantitatively genetic consistency between mother and daughter cells. 7. Uncontrolled mitosis causes cancer.
